title: Adaptive quant batching operational scenarios Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This sheet collates operational scenarios for adaptive quantization + batching policies across regions for Q3 2026. It is intended for SRE/Capacity planners and on-call engineers who will toggle precision/batching policies under load.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
We model three operational knobs — precision (fp16, int8, int4), batching window (10ms/50ms/200ms), and cross-region spill — to estimate required GPU headroom and expected end-to-end quality regressions per model group. For common production models, switching from fp16->int8 provides ~1.2–1.5x throughput with 0.5–2.5% expected quality degradation; int4 yields ~1.6–2.5x throughput with larger quality variance (1.5–6%). We recommend a staged automation: primary fallback to int8 + 50ms batching at 85% per-GPU utilization, and emergency int4 + 200ms batching only if tail latencies spike above SLA and error budgets are exhausted.

Assumptions & baseline metrics:
- GPU types in fleet: H100 (64GB), A100 (40GB).
- Baseline model group (chat-medium): avg request tokens = 120, avg response tokens = 80, tokens processed per request = 200.
- Measured baseline throughput (fp16, 50ms batching, H100): 12,000 tokens/sec (aggregate across batching).
- Measured baseline p50 latency (fp16, 50ms batching): 90ms. p95: 340ms.
- Batching efficiency: 50ms window ~0.82, 10ms ~0.35, 200ms ~0.95 for typical request-size distribution.
- Quality delta heuristics (estimated): fp16->int8: -0.5% to -2.5% depending on model; fp16->int4: -1.5% to -6%.

Scenario table (per-region, per-model-group):
Columns: Region | ModelGroup | Baseline GPUs (H100 equiv) | Traffic (rps) | Avg tokens/req | Target SLO p95(ms) | Policy @85% util | Est GPUs after policy | Est quality delta | Notes
Rows:
1) us-west | chat-medium | 120 | 35 | 200 | 500 | int8 + 50ms | 85 | -1.2% | expected headroom 10 GPUs for burst; enable prefix cache
2) eu-west | chat-medium | 60 | 18 | 200 | 600 | fp16 + 10ms (low-latency lane) | 60 | 0.0% | keep low-latency pool; shift overflow to int8 pool in us-east
3) ap-southeast | chat-medium | 24 | 8 | 200 | 800 | int4 + 200ms (emergency) | 12 | -3.8% | need cross-region spill policy to reduce customer impact
4) us-east | embedding-large | 80 | 6 | 8192 | 900 | int8 + 50ms | 48 | -0.7% | embeddings tolerate int8 for cost savings

(Notes on columns: Est GPUs after policy is derived from tokens/sec multipliers and batching efficiency; baseline GPUs are H100-equivalent computed from current fleet mix.)

Throughput multipliers & quality guide (summary):
- fp16, 50ms batching: baseline (1.0x throughput, 0% quality delta)
- fp16, 10ms batching: 0.6x (lower throughput, lower latency for small models)
- fp16, 200ms batching: 1.1x (better throughput, higher p95)
- int8, 50ms batching: 1.4x throughput, quality -0.5% to -2.5%
- int8, 200ms batching: 1.6x throughput, quality -0.7% to -3.0%
- int4, 50ms batching: 1.9x throughput, quality -1.5% to -5%
- int4, 200ms batching: 2.3x throughput, quality -2% to -6% (high variance)

Sample calculation (worked example):
Objective: compute GPUs needed for us-west chat-medium at 40 rps, avg tokens/req 200, target policy int8 + 50ms.
- Tokens/sec incoming = 40 rps * 200 tokens = 8000 tokens/sec.
- Effective per-H100 throughput at int8+50ms = baseline 12k tokens/sec * 1.4 = 16.8k tokens/sec (adjust for 0.82 batching efficiency -> effective 13.8k).
- GPUs required = ceil(8000 / 13800) = 1 H100-equivalent GPU. (rounded and then apply minimum shard size rules -> allocate 3 GPUs for shard granularity and headroom)
Operational runbook (high level):
1) Normal ops (<80% avg per-GPU util): keep fp16 default, 50ms batching.
2) Elevated (<90% util OR p95> SLA): auto-scale to int8 pool for overflow (policy threshold 85% sustained util over 5m).
3) Emergency (>95% util OR sustained errors): enable int4 + 200ms batching in emergency pool for up to 10 minutes while autoscaling completes.
4) Cross-region spill: if region A reaches emergency AND downstream latency < region B+50ms, redirect 20–40% of new requests to region B with int8 policy.
5) Quality monitoring: run lightweight A/B on 1% traffic when switching precision; rollback if eval metrics degrade >2x expected band.

Operational play triggers & SLOs:
- Trigger int8 pool: per-GPU CPU/GPU util > 85% for 5m AND p95 latency > 0.9 * SLA.
- Trigger int4 emergency: util > 95% for 3m OR errors/timed-out requests rate > 1% of traffic for 2m.
- Rollback: if user-facing eval metric fails by >3% absolute or error budget consumed >50% in 1h.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Quality variance: automated eval sets must be run for each model group before enabling int4. Mitigation: staged rollout + canary checks.
- Latency regressions with large batching windows: use latency-aware routing to keep 10ms lane for interactive clients (web UI).
- Regional capacity imbalance: maintain minimal cross-region buffer (˜10% of regional steady-state) to accept spill without immediate autoscale.

Action items (owners):
- Run end-to-end quality tests for chat-medium under int8/int4 (Diego) — due 2026-03-18.
- Implement policy toggles + monitoring alerts in control plane (Maya) — PR target 2026-03-22.
- Update incident runbooks and train on-call (Ethan) — runbook review 2026-03-24.
